rulings.challenge_claim: The alternative recorded as rejected for this span's ending (a close one verse earlier, at Lam.1.8) is markedly weaker than the live question the span's own discussion already raises, namely whether the first-person plea inside Lam.1.9 is itself the onset of the personified city's voice; that stronger rival is named in the discussion but never weighed as the alternative actually set against the chosen ending.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real but the framing is wrong. Bytes first: Lam.1.9 runs the contiguous refrain אֵ֥ין מְנַחֵ֖ם לָ֑הּ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier) and then the plea רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אֶת עָנְיִ֔י (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier), an imperative plus vocative followed by a first-person-singular noun -- refrain first, plea second, exactly the order the reading states. The acrostic letters run het at Lam.1.8 and tet at Lam.1.9, so a close at either verse sits on a letter boundary and both are lawful cuts under the tier-1 acrostic spine. That is what breaks the challenge's framing: inside this poem a row seam cannot fall mid-verse, so the rival the challenge calls omitted -- reading the Lam.1.9 plea as the onset of personified speech -- has exactly ONE lawful boundary form, a close at Lam.1.8, and that IS the alternative on record. No stronger unrecorded rival exists. What is genuinely defective is the ground the rejection rests on: it is argued from refrain mechanics alone (severing the refrain word from the report it closes) and never engages the voice-onset reading, and it weighs the candidate seam from one side only. Weighed from both sides, an undisclosed feature straddles this span's closing seam: the imperative-plus-vocative address to the deity רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier) stands inside the span and the same address form stands again inside Lam.1.11 outside it, so the tier-1 discourse frame the reading treats as the mark of a momentary intrusion runs on across its own cut. Severity stays low: the chosen close is carried by the tier-1 refrain and the span's content is unaffected.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative so the rejected close at web:Lam.1.8 is argued against the reading it actually expresses -- the first-person plea inside web:Lam.1.9 as the onset of the personified voice -- rather than against a refrain-mechanics point, and weigh the refrain close from both sides of that letter boundary. Add to device_notes a one-sentence disclosure that the imperative-plus-vocative address to the deity stands at web:Lam.1.9 and again at web:Lam.1.11, straddling this span's own closing seam. TEST: the rewritten alternative must survive a both-sides read of the Lam.1.8/Lam.1.9 letter boundary (both are letter boundaries; neither is a mid-verse cut) and must not rest on refrain mechanics alone; the straddle disclosure must name both verses.

rulings.challenge_claim: The discriminating ground offered for this span -- that verbs and pronouns stay third-person until the plea at the close of Lam.1.11 -- is contradicted by Lam.1.10, which addresses the deity in the second person; and the whole person-and-form argument is made with no Hebrew quoted anywhere, so nothing in it is testable at byte tier.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed on both arms. Lam.1.10 carries אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֔יתָה (oshb:Lam.1.10, byte tier), a second-person perfect with the paragogic ending, and לָֽךְ (oshb:Lam.1.10, byte tier), a second-person pronoun; the addressee is the deity, and both stand before the closing plea of Lam.1.11. The translation rendering the reading itself quotes carries the same datum in English, so the counter-evidence sits on the page while the opposite is asserted, and the rejected alternative repeats the same premise. A complete scan of this span's prose finds no Hebrew string anywhere in it: the person claim is argued entirely from a translation, a tier-4 witness that can never carry a form claim. Two qualifications set the severity at medium rather than high. First, the span's conclusion survives: a second-person address to the deity is an addressee feature, not a change of speaker, and no first-person-singular form stands in Lam.1.10 or before the plea that closes Lam.1.11, so the personified city's own voice is genuinely absent across the span. Second, the same imperative-plus-vocative address to the deity stands one verse behind the front seam at Lam.1.9, רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.1.9, byte tier), so under the both-sides law that tier-1 discourse frame straddles the front seam undisclosed rather than marking it.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative, replace the ground 'the verbs and pronouns stay third-person' with the ground the bytes support: no first-person-singular form stands until the plea that closes web:Lam.1.11, so the speaker is still the narrator. In the same fields disclose that web:Lam.1.10 addresses the deity in the second person (a second-person perfect and a second-person pronoun) and that the same imperative-plus-vocative address stands at web:Lam.1.9, straddling the front seam. Splice at least one pointed form from web:Lam.1.10 into boundary_rationale with its oshb: ref and byte tier named. TEST: run a complete person scan of web:Lam.1.10; the rewritten ground must survive it (the scan returns the second-person perfect and the second-person pronoun), and the row must carry at least one byte-tier Hebrew splice supporting its person claim.

rulings.challenge_claim: One continuous first-person city voice is asserted across Lam.1.12-Lam.1.17 and the unit is closed on the refrain inside Lam.1.17, but that closing verse carries no first-person form at all and describes Zion, Jacob and Jerusalem in the third person -- so the unit label, the refrain-close warrant and the high confidence are not carried by the bytes; a close at Lam.1.16 leaving Lam.1.17 as a third-person bridge is at least as well supported by the forms and is never weighed.
rulings.grounds: The two items are ONE defect reached from two sides, with a second distinct arm on calibration. Bytes: first-person-singular marking stands in every verse from Lam.1.12 through Lam.1.16 -- Lam.1.12 carries a first-person noun and a first-person prepositional form, Lam.1.13, Lam.1.14 and Lam.1.15 each carry first-person suffixes and first-person object suffixes, and Lam.1.16 opens with the first-person independent pronoun. A complete token scan of Lam.1.17 returns ZERO first-person-singular forms; that verse runs third-person feminine throughout, and its refrain is אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לָ֔הּ (oshb:Lam.1.17, byte tier), carrying the third-person feminine suffix -- the same suffix as at the first refrain site and not the first-person suffix that stands at the third site, אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Lam.1.21, byte tier). So the tier-1 refrain that closes this unit stands inside a narrator verse, not inside the city's speech, and both the unit label and the voice description fail at the span's last verse with no per-bytes deviation disclosed. The calibration arm is distinct and also holds: confidence is recorded high with the frontier flag not taken, on a span whose voice description fails at its closing verse. The unweighed alternative is real -- first-person marking resumes immediately at Lam.1.18 with מָרִ֑יתִי (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier; this verse carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed because a form is spliced from it) -- but a close at Lam.1.16 would leave Lam.1.17 standing alone on one letter, which the ruled granularity bars absent a disclosed tier-1 reason, and the verse cannot fold forward into the first-person span that follows; the disclosed-deviation cure, not a respan, is therefore the operative remedy. Severity high: three fields ride on the failed description.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes: add the one-sentence per-bytes deviation disclosure -- the span's closing verse carries no first-person-singular form and runs third-person feminine, and the refrain that closes the unit there carries the third-person feminine suffix, against the first-person suffix at the third refrain site. (2) confidence: lower from high to medium_low, and set frontier_flag_considered true. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the Lam.1.18-extension alternative with the live rival -- a close at web:Lam.1.16 leaving web:Lam.1.17 as a third-person bridge -- and record why it is not taken (a single-letter unit at web:Lam.1.17 is barred by the ruled granularity, and the verse cannot fold forward into the first-person span that follows). (4) observed_substrate_signals: keep the refrain key and add a voice key that names the third-person bridge instead of an unbroken city voice. TEST: run a complete person scan of the span's closing verse; the voice description, the unit_type value and the confidence must all survive it (the scan returns zero first-person-singular forms), and no field may assert an unbroken first-person voice through that verse without the disclosure.

rulings.challenge_claim: The opening line frames the personified voice as continuing across the refrain in the preceding verse into this span, but that preceding verse carries no first-person form -- it names Zion, Jacob and Jerusalem in the third person only -- so the transition claim borrows a continuity the bytes do not support, even though the span's own content and close stand on independent grounds.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed and correctly scoped. A complete token scan of the front-seam neighbour Lam.1.17 returns zero first-person-singular forms; that verse is third-person feminine throughout. The span's own first verse opens the first person afresh with מָרִ֑יתִי (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier; this verse carries a ketiv/qere note on the word rendered as the peoples, disclosed because a form is spliced from it). So the voice RESUMES after an intervening third-person verse; it does not keep speaking across it, and the front-seam sentence as written asserts the stronger of the two. This is a field defect distinct from the same underlying byte fact adjudicated on the neighbouring span, and low is the right grading: the span's content is first-person throughout and its close rests on independent tier-1 grounds that verify -- the third refrain site carries the first-person suffix אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Lam.1.21, byte tier) against the third-person feminine suffix at the two earlier sites (sweep: 3 verses for the contiguous two-token refrain form), and the poem's own letter run closes at Lam.1.22. One further byte finding on the same fields, not raised in the challenge: the rejected split is defended as an over-fine cut inside one sustained address to the deity, but the span does not open on an address to the deity -- Lam.1.18 carries שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier), a second-person PLURAL imperative addressed to the peoples; the sustained second-person-masculine-singular address to the deity runs Lam.1.20-Lam.1.22 only.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: reword the opening transition so the first-person voice RESUMES at web:Lam.1.18 after an intervening third-person verse, and disclose the front-seam neighbour's person state (no first-person-singular form at web:Lam.1.17). (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: narrow 'one sustained address' to web:Lam.1.20-web:Lam.1.22, and record that the span opens instead on a second-person plural imperative appeal to the peoples at web:Lam.1.18. TEST: the transition sentence must survive a person scan of the front-seam neighbour (zero first-person-singular forms there) and of the span's first verse (the first-person perfect present); the rejected-alternative sentence must survive an addressee scan of web:Lam.1.18 (a plural imperative to the peoples, not to the deity).

rulings.challenge_claim: The span rejects an interior split on the ground that a topic change alone is not a seam, then draws its own closing seam at Lam.2.9/Lam.2.10 on exactly that kind of ground -- no voice or addressee change stands at the seam -- while the mark layer cited for the edge stands at every verse of this poem and cannot discriminate, and one of the span's own cited formulas runs across the seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: The finding holds; one supporting scan range in the challenge material is byte-false and is corrected here. Corrected range: a complete token scan of Lam.2.1 through Lam.2.10 -- not through Lam.2.12 -- returns no second-person form and no first-person-singular form; Lam.2.11 carries three first-person-singular forms, opening with עֵינַי֙ (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier), and Lam.2.12 runs third-person plural. With that correction the operative finding stands exactly: no person or addressee change marks the Lam.2.9/Lam.2.10 seam, the nearest byte-marked voice change stands one verse past it, and Lam.2.10 continues third-person plural narration of the mourners. The interior split is set aside on the standard that a topic change alone is not a seam, and the closing seam meets no better standard than the one rejected -- what changes there is the subject matter and the grammatical subject, from the deity's action against the city's institutions to the mourners' response, not the tier-1 voice or addressee classes. The undisclosed straddle is byte-true: the daughter-of-Zion formula stands at בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.8, byte tier) inside the span and again at בַת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.10, byte tier) immediately outside it (sweep: 8 verses book-wide for the two-token phrase), so a device the span itself cites argues continuity across its own cut. The mark layer cannot carry the edge either: the same mark type stands at every verse of this poem, so it is non-discriminating as well as tier-3 weak single-witness. Severity is set at medium, above the lower of the two gradings: this is the span's own boundary, and both the asymmetric standard and the undisclosed straddle bear directly on it.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: state the actual ground for the closing seam -- the shift from the deity's action against the city's institutions to the third-person report of the mourners, with the first-person onset standing one verse past the seam -- and stop resting the edge on the mark layer, which stands at every verse of this poem and cannot discriminate one cut from another. (2) device_notes: disclose that the daughter-of-Zion formula stands on both sides of the closing seam, at web:Lam.2.8 and web:Lam.2.10, and argues continuity against the cut. (3) PROPOSAL for boss adoption only, not a work order: move the close to web:Lam.2.10 so the seam sits at the first-person onset in web:Lam.2.11 -- a letter boundary (yod at Lam.2.10, kaf at Lam.2.11), inside one poem parent, straddling no poem seam -- with the neighbouring span's front seam moved to match; adopt only if the boss rules the first-person onset the stronger edge. TEST: the seam ground must survive the same standard the row applies to its rejected interior split (a topic change alone is not a seam); a complete person scan of web:Lam.2.1-web:Lam.2.10 must return zero first-person-singular and zero second-person forms with the first-person onset located at web:Lam.2.11; the straddle disclosure must name both verses.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit label names a closing turn to direct address although three of the four verses carry no addressee at all and no deviation is disclosed; one cited sweep digit is attached to the wrong swept object (a three-token daughter-formula credited with the two-token pattern's count); and the second-person feminine singular address chain, together with a second daughter-formula, runs across the closing seam undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Four arms, all byte-confirmed; the two items converge on the label arm and one carries the rest, so they are distinct defects on one row. Label: Lam.2.10 runs third-person plural (the elders, their heads), Lam.2.11 turns to the narrator's own first person with עֵינַי֙ (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier) and two further first-person forms, Lam.2.12 runs third-person plural again, and only Lam.2.13 carries addressee marking, opening with אֲעִידֵ֞ךְ (oshb:Lam.2.13, byte tier), a second-person feminine singular form. The operative-category law permits a per-bytes deviation with a one-sentence disclosure in device_notes; device_notes carries no such disclosure, and the held question that IS recorded holds open where the address begins, not that the whole span is labelled from its closing verse. Digit: the three-token phrase בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת צִיּ֑וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.13, byte tier) stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse); the figure of 2 belongs to the two-token pattern, whose other site is לִבְתוּלַ֖ת בַּת יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Lam.1.15, byte tier) -- a different daughter-name, and there behind a single tolerated prefix letter (sweep: 2 verses for the two-token pattern). Object and digit do not match, which is precisely the phrase-test trap these formulas carry. First straddle: a complete enumeration of this poem's second-person feminine singular forms puts them in exactly 7 consecutive verses, Lam.2.13 through Lam.2.19, and in no other verse of the poem (sweep: 7 verses), so the closing seam cuts that tier-1 chain at its first joint and the address argues continuity across the cut rather than marking it. Second straddle: the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula stands at הַבַּת֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Lam.2.13, byte tier) inside the span and at בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Lam.2.15, byte tier) outside it (sweep: 2 verses book-wide) -- the digit is right, the straddle undisclosed. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-attach the digit to its object -- cite the three-token virgin-daughter-of-Zion phrase as 'sweep: 1 verse book-wide', and if the figure of 2 is kept, attach it to the two-token virgin-daughter pattern and name both sites and the different daughter-name at the other one. (2) device_notes: add the one-sentence per-bytes deviation disclosure for the operative category (three of the four verses carry no addressee marking; the label rides on the closing turn), and disclose the two devices that run across the closing seam -- the second-person feminine singular addressee chain running web:Lam.2.13-web:Lam.2.19, and the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula at web:Lam.2.13 and web:Lam.2.15. (3) unit_type: keep apostrophe_address only if the disclosure in (2) is carried; otherwise reclassify to the category the first three verses support. TEST: every sweep digit must name the swept object it counts (the three-token phrase returns 1 verse, the two-token pattern returns 2); a token scan of the span's first three verses must return zero addressee marking and the unit label must carry a disclosure that survives it; each straddle disclosure must name both sides of the seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span's sole boundary ground -- that the address to the daughter of Jerusalem gives way at its first verse to a third-person report -- is inverted relative to the pointed text: all four verses address the city in the second-person feminine singular, so the unit label and the third-person-narrator signal key are unsupported at every verse; both seams cut the address chain undisclosed, and no Hebrew is quoted anywhere in the grounds.
rulings.grounds: One defect, reached independently from both sides, and the strongest in this cluster. Every verse of the span carries second-person feminine singular addressee marking: נְבִיאַ֗יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.14, byte tier; this verse carries a ketiv/qere note, disclosed because a form is spliced from it), עָלַ֤יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.15, byte tier), א֣וֹיְבַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.16, byte tier), צָרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.17, byte tier). A complete enumeration of this poem's second-person feminine singular forms returns exactly 7 consecutive verses, Lam.2.13 through Lam.2.19, and no other verse of the poem (sweep: 7 verses); the span sits wholly inside that chain. What actually changes at the front seam is the speaker's self-reference, not the addressee: the first-person verbs of Lam.2.13, אֲעִידֵ֞ךְ among them (oshb:Lam.2.13, byte tier), drop out while the addressee marking runs on unchanged. Third-person finite verbs with a second-person addressee are not a third-person report, so the unit_type value and the third-person-narrator signal key fail at every verse of the span, and the rejected alternative rests on the same inversion. Both seams cut the chain undisclosed: at the front the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula stands on both sides (oshb:Lam.2.13 and oshb:Lam.2.15, sweep: 2 verses book-wide), and at the back the addressee marking runs straight on into Lam.2.18 and Lam.2.19. The span also quotes no Hebrew at all, so a person claim about the source text is made with no byte-tier evidence. What holds and must be preserved in any repair: the letter disclosure nun, samekh, pe, ayin is byte-correct and naming pe before ayin as this witness's own order rather than an error to be corrected is right (tier-1 acrostic spine); the mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed; the ketiv/qere note at Lam.2.14 is disclosed; the taunt in the third verse is correctly read as the enemies' own quoted words; all translation renderings verify verbatim. Severity high.
rulings.remedy: (1) unit_type: replace city_lament with the operative category the bytes support (apostrophe_address); if city_lament is kept, device_notes must carry the one-sentence per-bytes deviation disclosure. (2) observed_substrate_signals: drop the third-person-narrator voice key and carry an address key naming the second-person feminine singular addressee marking. (3) boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: restate the front-seam ground as the drop of the speaker's first-person self-reference at web:Lam.2.14 while the addressee marking continues, and disclose both straddles -- the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula at web:Lam.2.13 and web:Lam.2.15, and the addressee chain continuing into web:Lam.2.18-web:Lam.2.19. (4) Splice at least one pointed second-person feminine singular form into boundary_rationale with its oshb: ref and byte tier named. (5) PROPOSAL for boss adoption only, not a work order: re-span the address chain as one unit, web:Lam.2.13-web:Lam.2.19 -- both edges are letter boundaries (lamed/mem at Lam.2.12/Lam.2.13, qof/resh at Lam.2.19/Lam.2.20), it sits inside one poem parent and straddles no poem seam, and it would absorb the neighbouring apostrophe spans; adopt only if the boss rules the unbroken addressee chain the governing seam class. TEST: run the complete enumeration of this poem's second-person feminine singular forms; the voice description, the unit_type value and every signal key must survive it (the enumeration returns web:Lam.2.13-web:Lam.2.19, seven consecutive verses), and no field may describe the span as a third-person report without the disclosure.

rulings.challenge_claim: The letter disclosure places this poem's pe-before-ayin swap LATER than Lam.2.18-Lam.2.19 when the swapped pair stands one and two verses BEHIND the span; the addressee options held open include one the pointed bytes exclude (the speaker's own heart); the second-person feminine singular address already runs across the front seam undisclosed; and the span quotes no Hebrew at all while the ketiv/qere note it calls unengaged sits on the very word its quoted rendering carries.
rulings.grounds: All four arms byte-confirmed. Letter order: the verse-initial consonants run pe at Lam.2.16 and ayin at Lam.2.17 -- the sixteenth and seventeenth positions, one and two verses BEHIND this span -- then tsade at Lam.2.18 and qof at Lam.2.19. The swapped pair is therefore behind the span, and calling it later in the poem is byte-false against the tier-1 acrostic spine; the claim it qualifies, that the span's own two letter positions are untouched by the swap, is correct and should be kept. Addressee: Lam.2.18 opens צָעַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier), a third-person singular perfect whose subject is a masculine noun carrying a third-person PLURAL suffix, while the commands that carry the stretch are second-person feminine singular throughout -- הוֹרִ֨ידִי (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier) and the four imperatives of Lam.2.19 -- which that noun cannot govern; the speaker's-own-heart option is excluded at the bytes, while the two feminine candidates inside the wall-of-the-daughter-of-Zion chain are correctly left open, the pointed text not separating them. Both sides of the front seam: second-person feminine singular address to the city is already running behind the seam at צָרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.17, byte tier) and continues through the span, an undisclosed straddling device -- what is new at Lam.2.18 is the imperative MOOD, not the addressee, so the seam holds on a narrower ground than the one stated. Variant: the ketiv/qere note at Lam.2.19 sits on בַלַּ֗יְלָה (oshb:Lam.2.19, byte tier), the qere reading of the very word the span's quoted rendering carries as the night, so calling the variant unengaged understates it. One further byte finding not raised in the challenge: the span's first verse is described as a turn to direct imperative address, but its opening clause is still third-person report and the imperative onset is verse-internal, so that description should be scoped to the clause rather than the verse. What holds: the mark type at Lam.2.17, Lam.2.18 and Lam.2.19 is single-witness and never conflated; the one paseq segment at Lam.2.19 is cited as a bare count; the ketiv/qere note is disclosed; the letters tsade and qof are correct; the translation renderings verify verbatim. Severity medium.
rulings.remedy: (1) device_notes: correct the letter-order sentence -- the swapped pair stands BEHIND this span at the sixteenth and seventeenth letter positions (web:Lam.2.16 and web:Lam.2.17), not later in the poem -- and keep the correct statement that the span's own two letter positions are unaffected. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative and boundary_rationale: drop the speaker's-own-heart addressee option (the heart in that verse carries a third-person plural suffix and stands as subject of a third-person singular verb, while the imperatives are second-person feminine singular) and keep the two feminine candidates open. (3) boundary_rationale: narrow the front-seam ground from the onset of address to the onset of the imperative mood, and disclose that second-person feminine singular addressee marking already runs at web:Lam.2.17 and continues through the span. (4) boundary_rationale: scope the turn to direct imperative address to the clause, since the opening clause of web:Lam.2.18 is still third-person report. (5) Restate the ketiv/qere disclosure so it records that the quoted rendering for web:Lam.2.19 stands on the qere word, and splice at least one pointed form with its oshb: ref and byte tier named. TEST: the letter-order sentence must survive a read of this poem's letter sequence at the sixteenth and seventeenth positions; each retained addressee option must survive a form check of the verse's opening clause and of the imperatives; the front-seam disclosure must name the verse behind the seam that already carries the addressee marking; the ketiv/qere sentence must survive a check that the quoted rendering and the qere word coincide.
